clinician.final_diagnosis: chronic nonunion of a medial condyle fracture
clinician.trajectory_summary: A six-year-old male presented with a dislocated left elbow which was successfully reduced closed without fracture visible on initial post-reduction x-rays. At six weeks, x-rays showed ossification near the medial epicondyle suggestive of injury sequelae without evidence of acute fracture. Five years later, the patient developed intermittent medial elbow pain, mild tenderness, and limited range of motion without any further trauma history. These clinical symptoms alongside early imaging ossification changes support the development of a chronic nonunion of a medial condyle fracture not initially identified.
